solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wearing precious stones and nothing else is wrong

parts.note: to be wearing clothes is to be in them
'just' as in merely, with nothing else besides
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone decked out in jewels and nothing more is behaving improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue: IN, then JUST (nothing else), then ICE (precious stones).
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong, as a noun, is an unfair act or grievance done to someone.

clue.text: Spin around, lacking velocity still

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter for velocity is dropped

parts.note: to invert is to turn something upside down or around
v is the physics symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A spinning object loses its speed and comes to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb but is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless, without power of movement, so it is a synonym of still.

clue.text: Something articulated about remedy for politicians' proposal

parts.note: an articulated thing is jointed, so a joint is something articulated
re means about or concerning
a solution is a remedy for a problem

explanation.surface: A jointed contraption is offered as the cure for something.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US Congress, this is a measure passed by both houses together, a legislators' motion.

clue.text: Eat basil in a stew, potentially getting full

indicators.note: in a stew means agitated and mixed up, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating basil cooked in a stew might fill you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satiable can be satisfied, so it is capable of being filled up.

clue.text: Key passage without its opening note

indicators.note: the passage word loses its opening letter, which here is a musical note

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: A musical key passage begins without its first note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is not musical: it means a low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, or cay, is a small low island, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: English skill behind film's sound engineering device

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion
the rump is the behind or bottom
ET is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: An English expert works behind the scenes on a film's sound engineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound engineering' suggests studio work, but the device engineers sound into a deaf ear.
explanation.definitionFit: This horn-shaped instrument amplified sound for the hard of hearing before hearing aids.

clue.text: What's swallowed by staff about to provide treatment

indicators.note: a thing swallowed goes inside, so the exclamation sits within the staff
about means turned round, so the staff word is read backwards

parts.note: a bar is a rod or staff
eh is a querying exclamation like 'what?'

explanation.surface: Something swallowed by a member of staff is offered as treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation is treatment for addiction or recovery from injury.

clue.text: Guide was in touch with royalty

parts.note: rang means telephoned, making contact
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A tour guide was in contact with members of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a Ranger is a senior member of the Girl Guides; also a park warden who guides visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest or park warden leads and directs visitors, so serves as a guide.

clue.text: Drink port, 24″ bottles, and move clumsily

parts.note: to have a drink is to consume it

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the side of a ship goes within the length

parts.note: twenty-four inches is two feet
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A drinker of port, sinking two-foot bottles, staggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' and 'bottles' look like the drinking theme, but port is the nautical left and bottles is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for dancing or moving awkwardly, lacking coordination.

clue.text: US money and yen received, clutching a buck

parts.note: a bill is an American banknote
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

indicators.note: clutching means holding tightly, so the received word holds the a inside

parts.note: got means received

explanation.surface: Dollars and yen are received, with someone gripping a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buck' looks like more US money, but it is the male animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is a male of certain animals, and a male goat is one example.

clue.text: The work of a man of letters?

definitions.text: The work of a man of letters?

parts.words: The work of a man of letters?
parts.note: a man of letters is a writer, but here also one who writes letters: a book told as correspondence

explanation.walkthrough: A 'man of letters' is normally a literary figure; the second reading is a novelist writing in the form of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This genre tells its story through a series of letters, so it is literally a work built of letters.

clue.text: Quartet's cover of tune with musical style

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: A string quartet does a cover version of a tune in a jazz style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' suggests a cover version in music; here it means the tune's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrad is a group or set of four, as a quartet is.

clue.text: Lets rip violently, Yankee, like father

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American lets rip in a violent outburst, just like his father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' is a priest, not a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is addressed as Father, so being like a father is behaving like a cleric.

clue.text: Scot waggles bum, meeting countryman?

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are wrongly arranged

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish name, so a countryman of the Scot, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A Scotsman wiggles his backside when meeting a man from the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a backside but is the anagram signal; the question mark shows IAN is just an example of a fellow Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Glasgow is a Scot, so this is a specific example.

clue.text: John, punched by cad, gets shiner: this hinders movement

indicators.note: punched by means pierced, so the cad goes inside the John

parts.note: a john is slang for a toilet, abbreviated WC
a heel is a cad, a dishonourable man
a lamp is something that shines

explanation.surface: A man named John is punched by a scoundrel and gets a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shiner' suggests a black eye but here is a light; 'John' is the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: This device locks onto a parked car's tyre, immobilising the vehicle until a fine is paid.

clue.text: Wicked bats flew round

indicators.note: bats means crazy, signalling the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Evil bats flew round in the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' is slang praise, not evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked in slang means excellent or great, a synonym of marvellous.

clue.text: American's not eating in country

definitions.meaning: in the US, food bought as a takeaway rather than eaten on the premises

explanation.surface: An American refuses to eat in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: This republic in West Africa lies between Ghana and Benin; the other sense is US takeaway food.

clue.text: Drive away from route through European mountains

indicators.note: a route passing through goes inside, so the street sits within the other pieces

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains
ST, street, is a route

explanation.surface: Someone drives away along a road running through Europe's mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to drive them away from a relationship.

clue.text: I won't and I will retreat

parts.note: no is a refusal, saying I won't
OK is an agreement, saying I will

explanation.surface: Someone first refuses and then agrees to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy corner is a retreat, a secluded place to withdraw to.

clue.text: Nitwits excited, receiving marks for test

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the marks go inside the excited word

parts.note: sent means thrilled or excited
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Excited fools are awarded marks for a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marks' suggests test scores but is the old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation of ability is a test, as in an exam or appraisal.

clue.text: Military group swims, coming up for a rest

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
dips are short swims

explanation.surface: An army unit goes swimming and emerges for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker and billiards a spider is a raised rest for the cue.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooker player uses this raised cue support, a type of rest, to bridge over balls.

clue.text: Provided drug, having made crack

parts.note: E is short for the drug ecstasy
a crack is a witty remark, so to make one is to quip

explanation.surface: Someone supplied drugs and was involved in making crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' suggests the drug, but it is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipped means furnished with what is needed, hence supplied.

clue.text: He'll go on record initially, interrupting old man

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the letter goes inside the father

parts.note: pater is old-fashioned slang for father, one's old man

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of record

explanation.surface: Someone will put it on record, cutting in on an old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go on' means talk on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who prates chatters at length, so he will go on and on.

clue.text: Grown son wearing nothing from Dior?

indicators.note: something being worn is inside, so the son letter is within the French word

parts.note: rien is French for nothing; Dior suggests France

explanation.surface: A grown-up son goes about wearing nothing designed by Dior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dior' is a French couture house, hinting the word for nothing is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Risen means got up or increased, as bread dough rises and grows.

clue.text: Seamstress may add one attention-seeking remark

parts.note: a means one
a seamstress sews a folded-over edge onto a garment

explanation.surface: A dressmaker might include an extra item.
explanation.definitionFit: This throat-clearing sound is made to attract notice, an interjection seeking attention.

clue.text: Communist Chinese dish, mostly poultry, takes shape

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the dish

parts.note: fried rice is a Chinese dish
a hen is a domestic fowl
gels means sets or takes shape

explanation.surface: A Communist's Chinese meal, mostly chicken, comes together.
explanation.definitionFit: This German philosopher co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Marx.

clue.text: He hates company failure, changing central direction

indicators.note: the middle letter is a compass direction, south, swapped for another, north

parts.note: a loser is a failure

explanation.surface: A businessman hates the company's failure and changes its strategic direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' looks like a business; it means companionship.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person prefers to be alone, avoiding other people's company.

clue.text: Names covering brown walls of the famous residence

indicators.note: covering means surrounding, so the two letters for names enclose the rest

parts.note: N is short for name, so names is NN
umber is a brown pigment

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: Names cover brown walls in a famous house.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER TEN Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's London home.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister's official London home is a celebrated address.
